title: Day 2 Teaching Lab — Architecture Review Board
objective: Study-guide review — Day 2 — Secure Architecture, Cloud, and Resilience: Day 2 Teaching Lab — Architecture Review Board.

blocks.text: Scenario: a team is moving a customer-facing application to a hybrid cloud architecture. The application uses third-party packages, a CI/CD pipeline, containers, APIs, cloud storage, and a legacy on-premises database that cannot be replaced this quarter.
Ask students to review the design in five passes:

rows: Security, privacy, logging, availability, and audit requirements
Dependencies, package monitoring, build artifact integrity, vendor risk
Data movement, connectivity, identity federation, logging, encryption
Customer-owned IAM, storage configuration, secrets, application security
Load balancing, backup/restore, integrity validation, EOL compensating controls

items: CI/CD identities are privileged and need least privilege, review, logging, and rollback.
IaC improves consistency but can scale misconfiguration.
Cloud storage security requires key management, access control, monitoring, and retention.
The legacy database needs segmentation, monitoring, restricted access, and replacement planning.
Hybrid diagrams should be read as data-flow and responsibility maps, not only network drawings.
"The cloud provider handles security" fails shared responsibility.
"Add a load balancer" does not solve database resilience or data integrity.
"Scan the code before launch" is too late if requirements, pipeline identity, and dependency governance are missing.

blocks.text: Source: CertMaster Study Lessons 3A-3D; SecurityX M03 slides.

The official lessons list many controls: CASB, DLP, NAC, VPN, proxies, scanners, load balancers, CI/CD controls, container security, API security, and key management. Teach students to compose controls around the data flow. For example, a cloud-hosted API that processes confidential data may need API authentication, input validation, rate limits, logging, DLP/data classification, cloud IAM, key management, and CI/CD assurance. In practice questions, the answer often asks for the best next control, not every control, but the reasoning comes from understanding the whole flow.
